topSignals.title: Bloom Energy confirmed for S&P 500 inclusion effective Sept 21, 2026 — stock closed +7.35% and kept climbing after-hours.
topSignals.text: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced after Friday's close that Bloom Energy, Illumina, and Everpure will join the S&P 500, replacing Molson Coors, Trade Desk, and Builders FirstSource, effective before the open on Sept 21. BE closed the regular session at $252.87 (+$17.32/+7.35%, day range $235.55–253.30, 16.4M shares) on index-inclusion speculation already circulating that morning, then added another +5.25% after-hours to $266.14 once the announcement was confirmed. Market cap now ~$74.5B, comfortably clearing the size/liquidity/four-quarter-profitability screens S&P requires. This is the single biggest structural catalyst logged for Bloom this year: passive S&P-tracking funds (SPY, VOO, IVV and others) must now buy the stock, permanently deepening the shareholder base for the AI-datacenter SOFC bellwether. TipRanks | Barron's | Bloomberg

topSignals.title: EIA's August 2026 STEO directly confirms Henry Hub sub-$3.00/MMBtu through November — resolving yesterday's flagged gas-price discrepancy, and it cuts against the LCOE model's current assumption.
topSignals.text: Direct review of secondary reporting on the EIA's own August STEO shows futures through September 2026 held below $3.00/MMBtu, with EIA expecting the spot price to stay below $3.00/MMBtu until November 2026 and average just $3.03/MMBtu over the rest of the year (full-year 2026 average $3.44/MMBtu). That is materially below the $4.00–4.30/MMBtu the LCOE model currently carries and below the $3.91/MMBtu figure an older (Oct-2025-vintage) STEO citation had suggested. Recommend pulling the primary STEO PDF directly and revisiting the model's near-term gas-price input — a $3.00–3.44/MMBtu base case would meaningfully lower SOFC opex (and CCGT opex) versus what's currently modeled. EIA STEO PDF | Rigzone

topSignals.title: Virginia's first-in-the-nation data-center electricity tax starts accruing this month — and it taxes self-generated power too.
topSignals.text: The $0.011/kWh consumption tax (signed into the FY2027 budget in June, applying from July 1, 2026) requires its first monthly returns and payments in September 2026, per guidance the State Corporation Commission has been finalizing. The tax explicitly covers both utility-supplied and qualifying self-generated electricity, capped at $600M in annual statewide revenue with refunds above that. Relevant nuance for LCOE work: an on-site SOFC (or gas-turbine) installation serving a Virginia data center does not automatically escape this levy the way it might escape interconnection queues — worth a specific line item in any Virginia-sited deployment scenario. Williams Mullen | Greenberg Traurig
